# # Map customer Istio listener drain timing 503 spikes during xDS push to the Envoy ListenerManager / Istio Pilot ADS push-order boundary

A customer reports that during routine Istio Pilot config pushes their
service mesh sees brief 503 spikes for ~5 seconds on existing
connections, even for unchanged listeners. The spikes correlate with
ADS push events; the listener_manager logs show drain_in_progress
but no listener config actually changed.

Your task:
1. Find where Envoy's ListenerManager processes an LDS update and
   decides whether to drain existing listeners.
2. Find where Istio Pilot generates the ADS resource set and the
   ordering between LDS, RDS, CDS, and EDS resources for a config
   change.
3. Trace the cross-repo path: Pilot ConfigGenerator -> ADS Push ->
   Envoy XdsManager -> ListenerManager addOrUpdateListener ->
   ConnectionHandler drain. Cite each file and the function or
   attribute responsible.
4. Identify why Pilot's full-snapshot ADS push (vs delta-xDS) can
   send LDS resources with the same hash but a new version, causing
   Envoy to re-process them and trigger a drain even when nothing
   changed.


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4, github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1

I now have all the information needed for a complete, well-cited answer.

---

## Cross-Repo Path: Pilot ADS Push -> Envoy ListenerManager Drain

### 1. Envoy: LDS Update to Listener Drain

#### Subscription entry point: `GrpcMuxImpl::onDiscoveryResponse`

[`source/extensions/config_subscription/grpc/grpc_mux_impl.cc:264`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4/-/blob/source/extensions/config_subscription/grpc/grpc_mux_impl.cc?L264-336)

When Envoy's SotW ADS stream receives a `DiscoveryResponse`, `GrpcMuxImpl::onDiscoveryResponse` decodes each resource in the message and calls `processDiscoveryResources`, then dispatches to any registered `Watch` callbacks. For LDS, the registered watch callback is `LdsApiImpl`.

#### LDS callback: `LdsApiImpl::onConfigUpdate`

[`source/common/listener_manager/lds_api.cc:43`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4/-/blob/source/common/listener_manager/lds_api.cc?L43-141)

Two overloads exist:
- The **delta** overload (line 44) receives explicit add/remove sets.
- The **SotW** overload (line 122) computes removals itself by diffing current `WARMING | ACTIVE` listeners against the response set, then calls the delta overload.

For every resource in `added_resources`, it calls `listener_manager_.addOrUpdateListener(listener, resource.get().version(), true)` (line 93). Note: `resource.get().version()` is the **per-resource version string from the xDS response**, not a content hash.

Critically, before processing, it pauses RDS and SDS updates via `cm_.adsMux()->pause(...)` (line 53) — but does **not** suppress re-processing of an already-applied listener.

#### Hash-based deduplication: `addOrUpdateListenerInternal`

[`source/common/listener_manager/listener_manager_impl.cc:529`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4/-/blob/source/common/listener_manager/listener_manager_impl.cc?L529-628)

This is the critical function. At line 541:

```cpp
const uint64_t hash = MessageUtil::hash(config);
```

It then calls `blockUpdate(hash)` on any existing warming or active listener:

```cpp
// listener_impl.h:238
bool blockUpdate(uint64_t new_hash) { return new_hash == hash_ || !added_via_api_; }
```

[`source/common/listener_manager/listener_impl.h:238`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4/-/blob/source/common/listener_manager/listener_impl.h?L237-239)

**`blockUpdate` returns `true` (skip update) only if the proto hash matches the stored hash.** If `blockUpdate` returns `false` — meaning the hashes differ — the listener proceeds down the full update path (line 578–616), which:

1. Creates a new `ListenerImpl` (line 580).
2. Moves the existing active listener into `warming_listeners_` (line 599).
3. Calls `new_listener_ref.initialize()` to begin warming (line 626).

#### Drain triggered: `onListenerWarmed`

[`source/common/listener_manager/listener_manager_impl.cc:764`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4/-/blob/source/common/listener_manager/listener_manager_impl.cc?L764-794)

Once the warming listener completes (filter chain init), `onListenerWarmed` is called. At line 785–787:

```cpp
auto listener = std::move(*existing_active_listener);
*existing_active_listener = std::move(*existing_warming_listener);
drainListener(std::move(listener));
```

#### `drainListener`

[`source/common/listener_manager/listener_manager_impl.cc:640`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4/-/blob/source/common/listener_manager/listener_manager_impl.cc?L640-683)

The old active listener is moved to `draining_listeners_`. `stopListener` is called to stop accepting new connections, then `localDrainManager().startDrainSequence(...)` begins the drain timer. Existing connections continue to drain for the server-configured drain period (default: 45 s, `--drain-time-s`). During this window, Envoy may return 503s on connections that are mid-request when the connection handler shuts down their read filters.

---

### 2. Istio Pilot: ConfigGenerator -> ADS Push Ordering

#### ConfigGenerator interface

[`pilot/pkg/networking/core/configgen.go:27`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/networking/core/configgen.go?L27-50)

Defines `BuildListeners`, `BuildClusters`/`BuildDeltaClusters`, `BuildHTTPRoutes`. Each is implemented in `v1alpha3/`.

#### Generator registration

[`pilot/pkg/bootstrap/discovery.go:36`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/bootstrap/discovery.go?L36-68)

```go
generators[v3.ClusterType]  = &xds.CdsGenerator{ConfigGenerator: cg}
generators[v3.ListenerType] = &xds.LdsGenerator{ConfigGenerator: cg}
generators[v3.RouteType]    = &xds.RdsGenerator{ConfigGenerator: cg}
generators[v3.EndpointType] = edsGen
```

**LDS has no XdsCache entry.** CDS, RDS, EDS, and SDS all have cache entries (`XdsCacheImpl` at [`pilot/pkg/model/xds_cache.go:27`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/model/xds_cache.go?L27-32) covers `cds`, `eds`, `rds`, `sds` — no LDS type). `LdsGenerator.Generate` always calls `ConfigGenerator.BuildListeners` on every full push.

#### Full push: version bump

[`pilot/pkg/xds/discovery.go:254`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/discovery.go?L254-282)

```go
func (s *DiscoveryServer) Push(req *model.PushRequest) {
    if !req.Full {
        req.Push = s.globalPushContext()
        s.dropCacheForRequest(req)
        s.AdsPushAll(req)
        return
    }
    versionLocal := s.NextVersion()          // always increments
    push, err := s.initPushContext(req, oldPushContext, versionLocal)
    ...
    req.Push = push
    s.AdsPushAll(req)
}
```

[`pilot/pkg/xds/discovery.go:609`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/discovery.go?L609-611):

```go
func (s *DiscoveryServer) NextVersion() string {
    return time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339) + "/" + strconv.FormatUint(s.pushVersion.Inc(), 10)
}
```

**Every full push produces a new `PushVersion`, unconditionally.** This becomes the `VersionInfo` field of every `DiscoveryResponse` sent.

#### Push ordering: `PushOrder`

[`pilot/pkg/xds/ads.go:778`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/ads.go?L776-787):

```go
var PushOrder = []string{v3.ClusterType, v3.EndpointType, v3.ListenerType, v3.RouteType, v3.SecretType}
```

`pushConnection` at line 742 calls `pushDetails()` → `orderWatchedResources()` which orders watched resources per `PushOrder`. So for a full push, the sequence sent is: **CDS → EDS → LDS → RDS → SDS**.

#### Per-resource push: `pushXds` / `LdsGenerator.Generate`

[`pilot/pkg/xds/xdsgen.go:96`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/xdsgen.go?L96-188)

The `DiscoveryResponse` is built as:

```go
resp := &discovery.DiscoveryResponse{
    TypeUrl:     w.TypeUrl,
    VersionInfo: req.Push.PushVersion,   // global version, always new on full push
    Nonce:       nonce(req.Push.LedgerVersion),
    Resources:   model.ResourcesToAny(res),
}
```

[`pilot/pkg/xds/lds.go:96`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/lds.go?L96-109): `LdsGenerator.Generate` calls `BuildListeners` and wraps each listener as `protoconv.MessageToAny(c)`. There is no diff or hash comparison against the last-sent state here — the full set is always regenerated and sent.

---

### 3. Root Cause: Why Unchanged Listeners Trigger Drain

The bug lives at the intersection of two design decisions:

#### Pilot side: `VersionInfo` always changes, content never diffed

On a full push, Pilot assigns a new `PushVersion` (timestamp + counter) to every `DiscoveryResponse`, including the LDS response. Even if no listener configuration changed, `LdsGenerator.Generate` regenerates all listeners from scratch (no LDS caching) and sends them all in a response with the **new version string**. The response body — the listener protos — may be byte-for-byte identical to the previous push.

#### Envoy side: `blockUpdate` tests proto hash, but only against the stored listener hash

In `addOrUpdateListenerInternal` ([line 541–566](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4/-/blob/source/common/listener_manager/listener_manager_impl.cc?L541-566)), Envoy computes `MessageUtil::hash(config)` from the **proto bytes** and checks `blockUpdate(hash)`. This check correctly short-circuits when the proto content is identical — **but only if Envoy already has that listener in its active or warming state** with a matching hash.

#### The gap: `version_info` vs proto hash

The `LdsApiImpl::onConfigUpdate` (SotW overload, [line 122](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.29.4/-/blob/source/common/listener_manager/lds_api.cc?L122-141)) receives decoded resources. The `DecodedResourceImpl::fromResource` stores `message->version_info()` as the resource version. This version string is **not** what `blockUpdate` checks — `blockUpdate` checks the proto hash. So if the proto bytes are the same, `blockUpdate` will correctly return `true` and skip the update.

**The actual trigger is subtler:** Pilot's `initPushContext` calls `dropCacheForRequest` ([line 506](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/discovery.go?L506)), which calls `s.Cache.ClearAll()` when `ConfigsUpdated` is empty (e.g. a forced full resync). After cache clear, `BuildListeners` re-executes all listener construction, including `EnvoyFilter` patches. If any `EnvoyFilter` patch is non-deterministic (e.g. uses `time.Now()`, random UUIDs in metadata, or dynamically-resolved addresses), the re-generated listener proto will differ from the previously-active hash even though no user-visible config changed. This produces a new `MessageUtil::hash(config)` → `blockUpdate` returns `false` → the listener enters warming → the active listener is drained.

Additionally, **full pushes clear and rebuild the PushContext** ([line 262–272](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/discovery.go?L262-282)), which recomputes all service and sidecar scope relationships. Any sidecar scope or service reordering that changes list ordering in the listener proto (even ephemerally) will flip the hash.

---

### Mitigations

1. **Migrate to delta-xDS (ALPN `h2`)**: With delta xDS ([`pilot/pkg/xds/delta.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/delta.go)), Pilot sends only changed resources via `GenerateDeltas`. Envoy's `DeltaSubscriptionState::isHeartbeatResource` can further suppress no-op re-sends. Pilot explicitly notes SotW is the problematic path (`ads.go:730–733`).

2. **Ensure listener proto determinism**: Audit `EnvoyFilter` patches and `BuildListeners` for any non-deterministic fields (timestamps, map iteration order). Proto serialization order can silently change the `MessageUtil::hash` even with identical logical config.

3. **Tune drain parameters**: Reduce `--drain-time-s` and `--drain-strategy=immediate` on sidecars to shrink the 503 window when drains are unavoidable, at the cost of more abrupt connection closure.

4. **Pin `PILOT_ENABLE_EDS_DEBOUNCE` and incremental push scope**: Where possible, use `req.Full = false` incremental pushes (only EDS/RDS changes). `ldsNeedsPush` ([`lds.go:79`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/istio--1.21.1/-/blob/pilot/pkg/xds/lds.go?L79-83)) returns `false` for non-full pushes, suppressing LDS entirely when only endpoints change.
